problem.title: Scale Every Side
problem.statement: A triangle has side lengths 3, 4, and 5. Which side lengths describe a similar triangle made with scale factor 2?
hints: Apply the same multiplier to every side.
Check new divided by original for each position.

validationMethods: direct multiplication by two on all three sides
independent ratio audit of every option; only B has three ratios equal to two

problem.title: One Factor, Missing Side
problem.statement: Corresponding sides of two similar figures are 4 and 10. If another side of the first figure is 6, what is the corresponding side of the second?

problem.title: Carry the Vertex Order
problem.statement: Triangle DEF is similar to triangle XYZ in that order. DE=7, EF=5, and YZ=15. What is XY?
hints: D matches X, E matches Y, and F matches Z.
Use EF↔YZ to find the factor.

solutionSteps.title: Match and scale
solutionSteps.body: EF↔YZ gives k=15/5=3. Since DE↔XY, XY=7×3=21.

validationMethods: independent proportion DE/XY=EF/YZ gives 7/XY=1/3, hence 21; choices audited

problem.title: Scale Coverage
problem.statement: A figure of area 18 square units is enlarged by linear scale factor 4. What is the new area?
hints: Area receives the factor in two dimensions.

validationMethods: independent rectangle model: dimensions 3 and 6 become 12 and 24, areas 18 and 288; option audit

problem.title: Half-Size Copy
problem.statement: Two figures have equal corresponding angles and all corresponding lengths in ratio 1:2. Which statement is true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are congruent but not similar.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are similar but not congruent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are both similar and congruent.

hints: Equal angles and proportional lengths establish similarity.

solutionSteps.title: Separate the relations
solutionSteps.body: The common factor establishes similarity. Because corresponding lengths are unequal, the figures are not congruent.

validationMethods: definition audit for similarity and congruence
independent scale-factor check 1/2≠1 makes only choice B true

problem.title: Two Dimensions, Two Rules
problem.statement: A figure has perimeter 30 and area 80. A similar figure has linear scale factor 3/2. What are its perimeter and area?

validationMethods: dimension-specific factors k and k² give 45 and 180
independent ratio checks 45/30=3/2 and 180/80=9/4; option audit
